x.ASV: A Psalm. Oh sing unto Jehovah a new song; For he hath done marvellous things: His right hand, and his holy arm, hath wrought salvation for him.
x.Darby: A Psalm. Sing ye unto Jehovah a new song: for he hath done wondrous things; his right hand and his holy arm hath wrought salvation for him.
x.KJV: A Psalm. O sing unto the Lord a new song; for he hath done marvellous things: his right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory.
x.YLT: A Psalm. Sing ye to Jehovah a new song, For wonders He hath done, Given salvation to Him hath His right hand and His holy arm.

nt: Here, **his right hand and the arm of his holiness** represents God’s great power. The psalmist is using body parts to refer to God’s strength and ability to act. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [his great and holy power]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and his holy arm]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Make sure that your translation communicates that Yahweh is the one who saves his people; he is not the one who is saved. Alternate translation: [have saved his people]
The word **Sing**, along with all of the command forms in this psalm, is plural here, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

x.ASV: Jehovah hath made known his salvation: His righteousness hath he openly showed in the sight of the nations.
x.Darby: Jehovah hath made known his salvation: his righteousness hath he openly shewed in the sight of the nations.
x.KJV: The Lord hath made known his salvation: his righteousness hath he openly shewed in the sight of the heathen.
x.YLT: Jehovah hath made known His salvation, Before the eyes of the nations, He hath revealed His righteousness,

nt: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to everyone that he saves people]

Here, **eyes** represents the sight or observation of people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in full view of the nations]

Here, **the nations** represents the people of all the nations. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people of all the nations]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [that he is righteous]

x.ASV: He hath remembered his lovingkindness and his faithfulness toward the house of Israel: All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
x.Darby: He hath remembered his loving-kindness and his faithfulness toward the house of Israel: all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of ourGod.
x.KJV: He hath remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel: all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
x.YLT: He hath remembered His kindness, And His faithfulness to the house of Israel, All ends of earth have seen the salvation of our God.

nt: By **He remembers**, the psalmist does not mean that God could forget something, since God cannot forget anything. He means that God consistently knows and acts according to his covenant loyalty and faithfulness. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [He bears in mind]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **covenant loyalty** and **faithfulness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [that he has committed to love and to be faithful]

Here, **house** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So **the house of Israel** figuratively means all the people descended from the patriarch Jacob, who was also known as Israel. Alternate translation: [to the people of Israel]

The psalmist is referring to all of the earth by naming the extremes, **the ends of the earth**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [people all over the earth]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Make sure that your translation communicates that Yahweh is the one who saves his people; he is not the one who is saved. Alternate translation: [how our God saves people]
The psalmist is using this possessive form to mean the God whom the people worship. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [from the God whom we worship]

x.ASV: Make a joyful noise unto Jehovah, all the earth: Break forth and sing for joy, yea, sing praises.
x.Darby: Shout aloud unto Jehovah, all the earth; break forth and shout for joy, and sing psalms.
x.KJV: Make a joyful noise unto the Lord, all the earth: make a loud noise, and rejoice, and sing praise.
x.YLT: Shout to Jehovah, all the earth, Break forth, and cry aloud, and sing.

nt: Here, **all the earth** represents all the people who live on the earth. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all people on the earth]

By **burst into song**, the psalmist means that people should suddenly begin singing with great emotion. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. If not, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [express your joy by singing]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **joy**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [sing joyfully]

x.ASV: Sing praises unto Jehovah with the harp; With the harp and the voice of melody.
x.Darby: Sing psalms unto Jehovah with the harp: with the harp, and the voice of a song;
x.KJV: Sing unto the Lord with the harp; with the harp, and the voice of a psalm.
x.YLT: Sing to Jehovah with harp, With harp, and voice of praise,

nt: The psalmist is not referring to a specific **harp**. He means harps in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [with harps]

The psalmist repeats the phrase **with the harp** to emphasize its meaning. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [with the harp, yes, with the harp]

The psalmist is using this possessive form to describe singing that is characterized by being vocal rather than instrumental. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and with people singing]

x.ASV: With trumpets and sound of cornet Make a joyful noise before the King, Jehovah.
x.Darby: With trumpets and sound of cornet, make a joyful noise before the King, Jehovah.
x.KJV: With trumpets and sound of cornet make a joyful noise before the Lord, the King.
x.YLT: With trumpets, and voice of a cornet, Shout ye before the king Jehovah.

nt: Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the King, Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before]
Here, **shout** refers to joyfully cheering in front of Yahweh. Be sure that your translation does not communicate that this is angry shouting. Alternate translation: [raise a cheer]

x.ASV: Let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof; The world, and they that dwell therein;
x.Darby: Let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein;
x.KJV: Let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.
x.YLT: Roar doth the sea and its fulness, The world and the inhabitants in it.

nt: The psalmist is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and let its fullness roar]

By **its fullness**, the psalmist means all the creatures that live in the sea. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and everything that fills it]

The psalmist is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [let the world and the dwellers in it roar]

Here the psalmist is speaking of **the world** as if it were a living thing that could shout. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [let it be as though the world were shouting]

x.ASV: Let the floods clap their hands; Let the hills sing for joy together
x.Darby: Let the floods clap [their] hands; let the mountains sing for joy together,
x.KJV: Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together
x.YLT: Floods clap hand, together hills cry aloud,

nt: The psalmist is speaking of **rivers** as if they were living beings that could **clap palm**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Let it be as though the rivers clap palm]

The psalmist is using **clap palm** as a common expression of his culture to mean “clap their hands.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Let the rivers clap their hands]

The psalmist is speaking of **the mountains** as if they were living things that could **rejoice**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [let it be as though the mountains rejoice together]

x.ASV: Before Jehovah; for he cometh to judge the earth: He will judge the world with righteousness, And the peoples with equity.
x.Darby: Before Jehovah, for he cometh to judge the earth: he will judge the world with righteousness, and the peoples with equity.
x.KJV: Before the Lord; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity.
x.YLT: Before Jehovah, For He hath come to judge the earth, He judgeth the world in righteousness, And the people in uprightness!

nt: Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the King, Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the presence of]

Here, **the earth** represents the people who live on the earth. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people of the earth]

Here, **the world** represents the people who live in the world. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people in the world]

These two phrases **he will judge the world with righteousness** and **the peoples with fairness** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [he will judge the world with righteousness, yes, he will judge the peoples with fairness]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [righteously]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **fairness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [equally]

The psalmist is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and he will judge the peoples with fairness]
